title: Resumable streaming API: context deadline propagation, detach/reattach, and per-request retry policy
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Problem: current Go SDK streaming surface tightly couples a network-backed io-like stream to a single request context. Long-running client work (e.g., partial processing, UI disconnect/reconnect, mobile foreground/background) needs the ability to detach the local consumer from a server stream and later resume from the last acknowledged message. Additionally we need clearer rules for how context deadlines and cancellations propagate across goroutines and through retry/backoff logic to avoid leaked goroutines and surprising retry behavior.

Goal: implement a first-class resumable streaming abstraction in the Go SDK with: (1) Detach() to return a resumable token and stop local goroutines without cancelling server streams unnecessarily, (2) Resume(token) to re-establish a stream starting after the last acked offset, (3) deterministic propagation of context deadlines/cancellations across the lifecycle (initial request, background reconnect attempts, per-message processing), and (4) configurable per-request retry/backoff policy that respects the original deadline and avoids overshooting SLAs.

Scope: SDK surface + runtime client coordination only. Server-side support for resume tokens is assumed present (ENG-20245). This ticket implements client semantics, tests, examples, and migration guidance for customers.
acceptance_criteria: New Stream interface exposes Detach() (returns opaque resume token) and Close(); Resume(ctx, token) reattaches to stream and continues from last acked message.
Context deadlines passed into Resume/Read honor remaining time; Resume must fail fast if not enough time remains for a meaningful reconnect (configurable threshold).
Per-request retry/backoff respects parent context cancellation and remaining deadline; no background goroutine should remain after ctx cancel or Close().
Integration tests simulate client detach + server restart + resume; verify message ordering and no duplicates beyond allowed-at-least-once semantics.
Example added to godoc showing common patterns (UI disconnect/reconnect, server-side transient error handling).
Benchmarks show <5% CPU overhead for detach/attach compared to existing streaming path under normal conditions.
Design doc and API review approved by SDK leads and runtime team (links in activity).
activity: 2026-02-25 - Liam O'Connor: Triage complete. Scoped as SDK-only work dependent on server resume token support (ENG-20245). Assigned to Ava.

2026-02-27 - Ava Martinez: Spike implemented: prototype Detach() returns base64 resume token (sequence id + partition). Verified resume works against local runtime. Pushed sketch to https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/514

2026-03-02 - Review comment (Rohit Patel): prefer explicit Ack() API instead of implicit on Read() to avoid surprises when client crashes between processing and implicit ack. Raised trade-off: ergonomic vs safety.

2026-03-03 - Ava Martinez: Decision to support explicit Ack(msgID) and also an optional auto-ack mode behind StreamOptions.AutoAck = true for ergonomic cases. Documented in design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/confluence/go-sdk/resumable-streaming

2026-03-05 - QA (Maya Chen): wrote integration test harness (dockerized runtime) to simulate packet loss and server restart. Found a goroutine leak when Resume() retried with exponential backoff longer than ctx deadline. Filed follow-up fix in branch fix/ensure-backoff-cancels
2026-03-07 - Ava Martinez: Implemented context-aware backoff that aborts retries if ctx.Done() is closed or if ctx deadline < minReconnectWindow. Added unit tests for abort path.
2026-03-09 - PR feedback (SRE team): suggested adding observability hooks: reconnect attempts metric and last_resume_offset tag. Added counters and documented in console-telemetry-README.

2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Marked In Progress -> ready for broader review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/532. E2E test run: https://ci.redwood.ai/teams/go-sdk/pipelines/resumable-streaming/1234
notes: Trade-offs: Resume token simplicity (opaque token with offset) avoids schema coupling but makes server-side migrations harder. We chose opaque token for initial ship and will version tokens if we change server format.
Compatibility: customers using AutoAck semantics today will keep behavior if they continue to call StartStream with AutoAck=true. New explicit Ack API is additive.
Operational: added metrics - sdk.stream.reconnects, sdk.stream.resume_latency_ms, and sdk.stream.active_resumable_streams. Documented recommended alert thresholds in console-telemetry-README.
Follow-ups: (1) add a bounded in-memory resume-cache for mobile offline flows (ENG-20900), (2) server-side hardening for token revocation/expiration (ENG-20245).
